topic: Growth, Reproduction, Metabolism and Cellular Organisation
title: Is a Mule Alive? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A mule never has babies, and most worker bees never lay eggs, yet both are clearly alive. Diya asks: is making babies really a sign of life? This lesson tests four features of life one by one, with their exceptions.

You will see growth from inside by cell division (plants all life, animals up to a certain age) next to mountains and sand mounds that grow from outside. Reproduction runs live in four ways: budding in yeast, regeneration in Planaria, fragmentation of a filament and one cell splitting into two, then the exceptions (mules, worker bees, couples who cannot have children). Metabolism is broken down and built up inside a cell, and a reaction in a test tube turns out to be neither living nor non living. Then cellular organisation and response (a shoot bending to light, day length and breeding), a side by side comparison, a pause and think check, a worked example grid, the exam trap, an original NEET match the column question, a recap card and three questions. Note: this topic (What is living?) is from the older NCERT edition and is not in the current rationalised NCERT text.

This is Episode 3 of our PUC Biology series.
Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
